questions.stem: A man who works as a sewage cleaner comes to the emergency with complaints of fever, conjunctival suffusion and elevated WBC . Investigation of choice is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Microscopic agglutination test
  • THE HISTORY SUGGESTS leptospirosis which is commonly associated with sewage workers.
  • Rodents are the most important reservoir- rats commonest worldwide source.
  • Transmission occurs when people come into contact with infected animal urine,g. canoeing, swimming in lakes and rivers, farming, Sewage exposure.
  • It is primarily a disease of tropical and subtropical regions, and infection in temperate regions is uncommon.
  • Serology-the mainstay of diagnosis.
  • Commercial tests using genus specific antigens are used to screen sera, and positive reactions confirmed in a reference laboratory using the micro- agglutination test (MAT) with live Leptospira (killed have lower sensitivity).
    • The MAT detects agglutinating antibodies in patient serum and is relatively serovar- specific, so a large number of antigens must be tested.


Oxford textbook of infectious diseases and microbiology, edition 2, pg 340-341.

questions.stem: A resident of West Rajasthan presents with erythematous nodule on leg, h&e stain shows 2-4mu round cell with kinetoplast in phagocyte, diagnosis:
questions.solutionHtml:
Leishmania tropica
  • The history explains cutaneous leishmania and h&e explains the LD body.
  • The other options are incorrect.


oxford textbook of infectious diseases and microbiology, edition 2, pg 528.

Stool antigen
  • The diagnosis of rotavirus can be rapidly done by stool antigen test usually done by immunochromatographic test.
  • Rotavirus- Three antigenically distinguishable groups (A to C) cause the human disease.
  • Virtually all outbreaks worldwide are caused by group A organisms.
  • It is found worldwide.
  • Infectious dose — less than equal to 100 organisms.
  • Transmission is faeco- oral (contaminated food or water, direct contact, or inhalation of aerosol from vomit or faeces), and virus is shed for up to a week after symptom onset.


Oxford textbook of infectious diseases and microbiology, edition 2, pg 409-410.

questions.stem: A man from Bihar presents with fever, splenomegaly on microscopy organism with kinetoplast was seen . What's the agent?
questions.solutionHtml:
Leishmania donovani
  • The question explains a typical clinical picture of leishmania and typical microscopic LD body description. Bihar is an endemic area in India for visceral leishmania.


Oxford textbook of infectious diseases and microbiology, edition 2, pg 529.
